title.en: **in / on / at** — which one for time and place?
title.vi: **in / on / at** — dùng sao cho đúng?

hook.en: "See you in Monday!" Every A2 learner says this once. And it makes sense — in your head, Monday is inside the week. But English picked **on** for days, and you just have to learn the pattern.
hook.vi: "See you in Monday!" Bạn học A2 nào cũng từng nói câu này. Và nghe cũng hợp lý — trong đầu bạn, Monday nằm trong tuần. Nhưng tiếng Anh chọn **on** cho ngày, và bạn phải học theo quy tắc đó.
hook.ja: 「See you in Monday!」— A2学習者なら誰でも一度は言うフレーズです。頭の中では「月曜日は週の中にある」ので in が自然に感じられます。でも英語は曜日に **on** を選びました。これは理屈ではなく、パターンとして覚えるものです。
hook.id: "See you in Monday!" Setiap pelajar A2 pernah mengatakan ini. Dan masuk akal — di kepalamu, Monday ada di dalam minggu. Tapi bahasa Inggris memilih **on** untuk hari, dan kamu tinggal menghafal polanya.

why.en: Indonesian uses **di** for everything — **di rumah** (at home), **di Jakarta** (in Jakarta), **di hari Senin** (on Monday). One word does all the work. English split the job across three: **in** for enclosed spaces and large time periods, **on** for surfaces and days, **at** for specific points.
why.vi: Tiếng Indonesia dùng **di** cho mọi thứ — **di rumah** (ở nhà), **di Jakarta** (ở Jakarta), **di hari Senin** (vào thứ Hai). Một từ làm hết mọi việc. Tiếng Anh chia ra ba: **in** cho không gian kín và khoảng thời gian lớn, **on** cho bề mặt và ngày, **at** cho điểm cụ thể.
why.ja: インドネシア語の **di** は場所にも時間にも使える万能な前置詞です。**di rumah**（家に）、**di Jakarta**（ジャカルタに）、**di hari Senin**（月曜日に）— すべて **di** 一つで済みます。英語はこれを3つに分けました：**in** は囲まれた空間や大きな期間、**on** は表面や曜日、**at** は特定の一点です。母語にこの区別がないため、感覚で選べません。
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia menggunakan **di** untuk semuanya — **di rumah**, **di Jakarta**, **di hari Senin**. Satu kata mengerjakan semua. Bahasa Inggris membaginya ke tiga kata: **in** untuk ruang tertutup dan periode waktu besar, **on** untuk permukaan dan hari, **at** untuk titik spesifik.

pattern.en: **Time**: **on** + day (on Monday), **in** + month / year / season (in June, in 2026, in summer), **at** + clock time / holiday (at 7pm, at noon, at Eid). **Place**: **in** + large area (in Jakarta, in the park), **on** + street / floor / surface (on Jalan Sudirman, on the second floor, on the table), **at** + specific point (at the bus stop, at the door). **Transport**: **on** the bus, **on** the train, **on** the plane.
pattern.vi: **Thời gian**: **on** + ngày (on Monday), **in** + tháng / năm / mùa (in June, in 2026, in summer), **at** + giờ / ngày lễ (at 7pm, at noon, at Eid). **Nơi chốn**: **in** + khu vực lớn (in Jakarta, in the park), **on** + đường / tầng / bề mặt (on Jalan Sudirman, on the second floor, on the table), **at** + điểm cụ thể (at the bus stop, at the door). **Giao thông**: **on** the bus, **on** the train, **on** the plane.
pattern.ja: **時間**：**on** + 曜日（on Monday）、**in** + 月・年・季節（in June, in 2026, in summer）、**at** + 時刻・祝日（at 7pm, at noon, at Eid）。**場所**：**in** + 広い範囲（in Jakarta, in the park）、**on** + 通り・階・表面（on Jalan Sudirman, on the second floor, on the table）、**at** + 特定の地点（at the bus stop, at the door）。**交通機関**：**on** the bus, **on** the train, **on** the plane（乗り物は **on**）。
pattern.id: **Waktu**: **on** + hari (on Monday), **in** + bulan / tahun / musim (in June, in 2026, in summer), **at** + jam / hari libur (at 7pm, at noon, at Eid). **Tempat**: **in** + area luas (in Jakarta, in the park), **on** + jalan / lantai / permukaan (on Jalan Sudirman, on the second floor, on the table), **at** + titik spesifik (at the bus stop, at the door). **Transportasi**: **on** the bus, **on** the train, **on** the plane.

practice.en: Say each aloud and feel where the preposition lands: "I'll see you **on** Friday." "She was born **in** March." "The meeting is **at** 3pm." "He lives **in** Bandung." "I'm **on** the bus right now." "Wait **at** the front door." "We go to Bali **in** July." "She is sitting **on** the sofa."
practice.vi: Nói thành tiếng từng câu và cảm nhận vị trí của giới từ: "I'll see you **on** Friday." "She was born **in** March." "The meeting is **at** 3pm." "He lives **in** Bandung." "I'm **on** the bus right now." "Wait **at** the front door." "We go to Bali **in** July." "She is sitting **on** the sofa."
practice.ja: 声に出して前置詞の位置を体に覚えさせましょう：「I'll see you **on** Friday.」「She was born **in** March.」「The meeting is **at** 3pm.」「He lives **in** Bandung.」「I'm **on** the bus right now.」「Wait **at** the front door.」「We go to Bali **in** July.」「She is sitting **on** the sofa.」
practice.id: Ucapkan setiap kalimat dengan keras dan rasakan di mana preposisinya: "I'll see you **on** Friday." "She was born **in** March." "The meeting is **at** 3pm." "He lives **in** Bandung." "I'm **on** the bus right now." "Wait **at** the front door." "We go to Bali **in** July." "She is sitting **on** the sofa."

takeaway.en: **di** ≠ one English word. Learn each pattern as a fixed phrase: on Monday, in June, at 7pm, on the bus.
takeaway.vi: **di** không bằng một từ tiếng Anh duy nhất. Học mỗi mẫu như một cụm cố định: on Monday, in June, at 7pm, on the bus.
takeaway.ja: **di** を一つの英単語に置き換えることはできません。それぞれのパターンを決まったフレーズとして覚えましょう：on Monday, in June, at 7pm, on the bus。
takeaway.id: **di** ≠ satu kata dalam bahasa Inggris. Pelajari setiap pola sebagai frasa tetap: on Monday, in June, at 7pm, on the bus.

title.en: Simple past vs present perfect — **sudah** can mean both
title.vi: Quá khứ đơn vs hiện tại hoàn thành — **sudah** có thể mang hai nghĩa

hook.en: "I have eaten pho yesterday." If you're an Indonesian speaker, this sentence probably looks fine. **Sudah makan** translates to both "ate" and "have eaten." But in English, **yesterday** forces simple past — no present perfect allowed.
hook.vi: "I have eaten pho yesterday." Nếu bạn nói tiếng Indonesia, câu này nhìn có vẻ ổn. **Sudah makan** dịch ra cả "ate" lẫn "have eaten." Nhưng tiếng Anh, **yesterday** bắt buộc dùng quá khứ đơn — không được dùng hiện tại hoàn thành.
hook.ja: 「I have eaten pho yesterday.」— インドネシア語話者には自然に見える文です。**Sudah makan** は「食べた」も「もう食べた」も表せるからです。しかし英語では、**yesterday** のような特定の過去を表す語があると、現在完了は使えず、必ず過去形になります。
hook.id: "I have eaten pho yesterday." Kalau kamu penutur bahasa Indonesia, kalimat ini mungkin terlihat biasa saja. **Sudah makan** bisa diterjemahkan sebagai "ate" maupun "have eaten." Tapi dalam bahasa Inggris, **yesterday** memaksa simple past — tidak boleh pakai present perfect.

why.en: Indonesian uses **sudah**, **pernah**, **belum** with the same verb form — no tense change. English makes a sharp split: simple past for finished actions at a specific past time (**yesterday**, **last week**, **in 2019**, **ago**); present perfect for experiences, results, or actions with a present connection (**ever**, **never**, **already**, **yet**, **just**, **before**).
why.vi: Tiếng Indonesia dùng **sudah**, **pernah**, **belum** với cùng một dạng động từ — không đổi thì. Tiếng Anh phân biệt rõ: quá khứ đơn cho hành động đã kết thúc ở thời điểm cụ thể trong quá khứ (**yesterday**, **last week**, **in 2019**, **ago**); hiện tại hoàn thành cho kinh nghiệm, kết quả, hoặc hành động còn liên quan đến hiện tại (**ever**, **never**, **already**, **yet**, **just**, **before**).
why.ja: インドネシア語の **sudah**（もう〜した）、**pernah**（〜したことがある）、**belum**（まだ〜していない）は動詞の形を変えずに使えます。英語は明確に区別します：特定の過去の時点（**yesterday**, **last week**, **in 2019**, **ago**）があるときは過去形、経験や現在とのつながりがあるとき（**ever**, **never**, **already**, **yet**, **just**, **before**）は現在完了です。日本語の「〜た」も両方を表せるので、同じ罠にはまりやすいです。
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia menggunakan **sudah**, **pernah**, **belum** dengan bentuk kata kerja yang sama — tidak ada perubahan tense. Bahasa Inggris membedakan dengan tajam: simple past untuk tindakan selesai di waktu lampau spesifik (**yesterday**, **last week**, **in 2019**, **ago**); present perfect untuk pengalaman, hasil, atau tindakan yang masih berhubungan dengan sekarang (**ever**, **never**, **already**, **yet**, **just**, **before**).

pattern.en: **Specific past time → simple past**: "I ate pho yesterday." (NOT "I have eaten pho yesterday.") **Experience / result → present perfect**: "I have been to Bali." (no specific time) **Already, yet, just → present perfect**: "I have already eaten." "She hasn't called yet." "He has just arrived." **Since / for + present perfect**: "I have lived here for three years." "I have known her since 2019."
pattern.vi: **Thời gian cụ thể trong quá khứ → quá khứ đơn**: "I ate pho yesterday." (KHÔNG "I have eaten pho yesterday.") **Kinh nghiệm / kết quả → hiện tại hoàn thành**: "I have been to Bali." (không có thời gian cụ thể) **Already, yet, just → hiện tại hoàn thành**: "I have already eaten." "She hasn't called yet." "He has just arrived." **Since / for + hiện tại hoàn thành**: "I have lived here for three years." "I have known her since 2019."
pattern.ja: **特定の過去の時点 → 過去形**：「I ate pho yesterday.」（「I have eaten pho yesterday.」とは言わない）**経験・結果 → 現在完了**：「I have been to Bali.」（特定の時間なし）**already, yet, just → 現在完了**：「I have already eaten.」「She hasn't called yet.」「He has just arrived.」**since / for + 現在完了**：「I have lived here for three years.」「I have known her since 2019.」
pattern.id: **Waktu lampau spesifik → simple past**: "I ate pho yesterday." (BUKAN "I have eaten pho yesterday.") **Pengalaman / hasil → present perfect**: "I have been to Bali." (tidak ada waktu spesifik) **Already, yet, just → present perfect**: "I have already eaten." "She hasn't called yet." "He has just arrived." **Since / for + present perfect**: "I have lived here for three years." "I have known her since 2019."

practice.en: Try each pair aloud and hear the difference: "I **ate** pho yesterday." vs "I **have eaten** pho before." "She **went** to Surabaya last month." vs "She **has been** to Surabaya three times." "He **left** five minutes ago." vs "He **has just left**." The time word tells you which tense: specific past marker (yesterday, ago) → simple past. No specific time → present perfect.
practice.vi: Nói thành tiếng từng cặp và nghe sự khác biệt: "I **ate** pho yesterday." vs "I **have eaten** pho before." "She **went** to Surabaya last month." vs "She **has been** to Surabaya three times." "He **left** five minutes ago." vs "He **has just left**." Từ chỉ thời gian quyết định thì nào: dấu hiệu quá khứ cụ thể (yesterday, ago) → quá khứ đơn. Không có thời gian cụ thể → hiện tại hoàn thành.
practice.ja: 声に出してペアで練習し、違いを聞き取りましょう：「I **ate** pho yesterday.」vs「I **have eaten** pho before.」「She **went** to Surabaya last month.」vs「She **has been** to Surabaya three times.」「He **left** five minutes ago.」vs「He **has just left**.」時間を表す語がカギ：特定の過去（yesterday, ago）→ 過去形。特定の時間なし → 現在完了。
practice.id: Coba setiap pasangan dengan keras dan dengar bedanya: "I **ate** pho yesterday." vs "I **have eaten** pho before." "She **went** to Surabaya last month." vs "She **has been** to Surabaya three times." "He **left** five minutes ago." vs "He **has just left**." Kata waktu menentukan tense-nya: penanda lampau spesifik (yesterday, ago) → simple past. Tanpa waktu spesifik → present perfect.

takeaway.en: Time word decides the tense. Specific past (yesterday, ago, last week) → simple past. No specific time + still relevant → present perfect.
takeaway.vi: Từ chỉ thời gian quyết định thì. Quá khứ cụ thể (yesterday, ago, last week) → quá khứ đơn. Không có thời gian cụ thể + còn liên quan đến hiện tại → hiện tại hoàn thành.
takeaway.ja: 時を表す語が時制を決めます。特定の過去（yesterday, ago, last week）→ 過去形。特定の時間なし＋現在とのつながり → 現在完了。
takeaway.id: Kata waktu menentukan tense. Masa lampau spesifik (yesterday, ago, last week) → simple past. Tanpa waktu spesifik + masih relevan sekarang → present perfect.

question.en: Fill in the blank: I ___ to Bali three times.

explanation.en: No specific time + life experience → present perfect: **have been**.
explanation.vi: Không có thời gian cụ thể + kinh nghiệm → hiện tại hoàn thành: **have been**.
explanation.ja: 特定の時間なし＋人生経験 → 現在完了：**have been**。
explanation.id: Tanpa waktu spesifik + pengalaman hidup → present perfect: **have been**.

explanation.ja: **yet** は現在完了の否定を表します：**hasn't finished yet**。

question.en: Which sentence is correct?

explanation.en: **just** + present perfect (has/have + V3): **has just left** — for very recent actions.
explanation.vi: **just** + hiện tại hoàn thành (has/have + V3): **has just left** — cho hành động vừa mới xảy ra.
explanation.ja: **just** + 現在完了（has/have + 過去分詞）：**has just left** — つい先ほど起こった行動。
explanation.id: **just** + present perfect (has/have + V3): **has just left** — untuk tindakan yang baru saja terjadi.

question.en: Fill in the blank: I ___ here since 2019.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: I ___ here since 2019.

explanation.en: **since** + starting point → present perfect: **have lived** (started in 2019, still true now).
explanation.vi: **since** + điểm bắt đầu → hiện tại hoàn thành: **have lived** (bắt đầu từ 2019, đến nay vẫn đúng).
explanation.ja: **since** + 起点 → 現在完了：**have lived**（2019年に始まり、今も続いている）。
explanation.id: **since** + titik awal → present perfect: **have lived** (mulai tahun 2019, masih berlaku sekarang).

title.en: **make** vs **do** — two words where Indonesian has one
title.vi: **make** vs **do** — hai từ mà tiếng Indonesia chỉ có một

hook.en: "I did a mistake." "Can you make me a favor?" Both sound wrong to a native English speaker — but perfectly logical if your language uses one word for both. Indonesian **buat** or **lakukan** covers both. English draws a line.
hook.vi: "I did a mistake." "Can you make me a favor?" Cả hai câu đều sai với người bản xứ — nhưng lại rất hợp lý nếu tiếng mẹ đẻ của bạn chỉ dùng một từ cho cả hai. Tiếng Indonesia **buat** hoặc **lakukan** bao hết. Tiếng Anh vạch ranh giới rõ.
hook.ja: 「I did a mistake.」「Can you make me a favor?」— どちらもネイティブには不自然に聞こえますが、母語で一つの動詞で済む言語の話者には理屈が通ってしまいます。インドネシア語の **buat** / **lakukan** は両方をカバーします。英語は明確に線を引きます。日本語の「する」も同様に両方をカバーするので、日本語話者も同じ混乱をします。
hook.id: "I did a mistake." "Can you make me a favor?" Keduanya terdengar salah bagi penutur asli bahasa Inggris — tapi sangat masuk akal kalau bahasamu hanya pakai satu kata untuk keduanya. Bahasa Indonesia **buat** atau **lakukan** mencakup semuanya. Bahasa Inggris membuat batas yang jelas.

why.en: Indonesian **membuat** and **melakukan** overlap in ways that don't match English. English splits the work: **make** = creating, producing, or causing something (a cake, a decision, a mistake, a noise, money, progress). **do** = performing activities, tasks, or general work (homework, the dishes, business, a job, your best). The split is about the RESULT: if something concrete comes out of it, it's likely **make**.
why.vi: Tiếng Indonesia **membuat** và **melakukan** chồng chéo theo cách không khớp với tiếng Anh. Tiếng Anh phân chia: **make** = tạo ra, sản xuất, hoặc gây ra cái gì đó (bánh, quyết định, sai lầm, tiếng ồn, tiền bạc, tiến bộ). **do** = thực hiện hoạt động, nhiệm vụ, công việc chung (bài tập, rửa bát, kinh doanh, công việc, hết sức mình). Sự khác biệt nằm ở KẾT QUẢ: nếu có thứ cụ thể được tạo ra, thường là **make**.
why.ja: インドネシア語の **membuat**（作る）と **melakukan**（行う）の使い分けは、英語の make/do の区別とは一致しません。英語では：**make** = 何かを作り出す・引き起こす（ケーキ、決断、間違い、音、お金、進歩）。**do** = 活動・作業・タスクを行う（宿題、皿洗い、仕事、ベストを尽くす）。ポイントは「結果」— 具体的な何かが生まれるなら、たいてい **make** です。
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia **membuat** dan **melakukan** tumpang tindih dengan cara yang tidak cocok dengan bahasa Inggris. Bahasa Inggris membagi tugasnya: **make** = menciptakan, menghasilkan, atau menyebabkan sesuatu (kue, keputusan, kesalahan, suara, uang, kemajuan). **do** = melakukan aktivitas, tugas, atau pekerjaan umum (PR, cuci piring, bisnis, pekerjaan, yang terbaik). Pembagiannya tentang HASIL: kalau ada sesuatu yang konkret yang dihasilkan, kemungkinan besar pakai **make**.

pattern.en: **make**: make breakfast, make a plan, make a mistake, make money, make a noise, make progress, make a decision, make a difference, make a phone call, make an effort. **do**: do homework, do the dishes, do business, do well, do your best, do a good job, do nothing, do the shopping, do a favor. Special: **take** a photo, **take** a break, **take** a risk, **take** care, **take** medicine, **take** a test.
pattern.vi: **make**: make breakfast, make a plan, make a mistake, make money, make a noise, make progress, make a decision, make a difference, make a phone call, make an effort. **do**: do homework, do the dishes, do business, do well, do your best, do a good job, do nothing, do the shopping, do a favor. title.en: Adjective **before** noun — the opposite of Indonesian
title.vi: Tính từ **trước** danh từ — ngược với tiếng Indonesia

hook.en: "I bought a car red." "She has a bag beautiful." If you grew up speaking Indonesian, this word order feels completely natural — **mobil merah**, **tas cantik**. English is the exact opposite.
hook.vi: "I bought a car red." "She has a bag beautiful." Nếu bạn lớn lên nói tiếng Indonesia, trật tự từ này hoàn toàn tự nhiên — **mobil merah**, **tas cantik**. Tiếng Anh thì ngược lại hoàn toàn.
hook.ja: 「I bought a car red.」「She has a bag beautiful.」— インドネシア語で育った人には完全に自然な語順です。**mobil merah**（車 赤い）、**tas cantik**（バッグ きれいな）。英語はその正反対です。日本語も「赤い車」「きれいなバッグ」と形容詞が前に来るので、日本語話者にはむしろ英語の語順の方が自然かもしれません。
hook.id: "I bought a car red." "She has a bag beautiful." Kalau kamu besar dengan bahasa Indonesia, urutan kata ini terasa sangat alami — **mobil merah**, **tas cantik**. Bahasa Inggris justru kebalikannya.

why.en: Indonesian places the adjective **after** the noun — this is a deep rule. **Rumah besar**, **buku bagus**, **makanan enak**. English does the reverse: the adjective always goes **before** the noun — **a big house**, **a good book**, **delicious food**. This is a 180-degree flip, and it takes conscious practice to override the instinct.
why.vi: Tiếng Indonesia đặt tính từ **sau** danh từ — đây là quy tắc nền tảng. **Rumah besar**, **buku bagus**, **makanan enak**. Tiếng Anh làm ngược lại: tính từ luôn đứng **trước** danh từ — **a big house**, **a good book**, **delicious food**. Đây là sự đảo ngược 180 độ, cần luyện tập có ý thức để vượt qua bản năng.
why.ja: インドネシア語は形容詞を名詞の **後ろ** に置きます — これは深い文法ルールです。**Rumah besar**（大きな家）、**buku bagus**（良い本）、**makanan enak**（おいしい食べ物）。英語はその逆で、形容詞は常に名詞の **前** です。**a big house**, **a good book**, **delicious food**。これは180度の反転で、本能を上書きするには意識的な練習が必要です。
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia menempatkan kata sifat **setelah** kata benda — ini adalah aturan yang dalam. **Rumah besar**, **buku bagus**, **makanan enak**. Bahasa Inggris melakukan sebaliknya: kata sifat selalu di **depan** kata benda — **a big house**, **a good book**, **delicious food**. Ini pembalikan 180 derajat, dan butuh latihan sadar untuk melawan insting.

pattern.en: English: **adjective + noun** — always. "A red shirt" (NOT "a shirt red"). "A big house" (NOT "a house big"). "An interesting book" (NOT "a book interesting"). When you have multiple adjectives, the order is: opinion → size → age → color → origin → material → noun. Example: "A beautiful small old red Italian leather bag."
pattern.vi: Tiếng Anh: **tính từ + danh từ** — luôn luôn. "A red shirt" (KHÔNG "a shirt red"). "A big house" (KHÔNG "a house big"). "An interesting book" (KHÔNG "a book interesting"). Khi có nhiều tính từ, thứ tự là: ý kiến → kích thước → tuổi → màu sắc → nguồn gốc → chất liệu → danh từ. Ví dụ: "A beautiful small old red Italian leather bag."
pattern.ja: 英語：**形容詞 + 名詞** — 常にこの順番です。「A red shirt」（「a shirt red」ではない）。「A big house」（「a house big」ではない）。「An interesting book」（「a book interesting」ではない）。複数の形容詞がある場合の順番は：意見 → サイズ → 年齢 → 色 → 原産地 → 素材 → 名詞。例：「A beautiful small old red Italian leather bag.」
pattern.id: Bahasa Inggris: **kata sifat + kata benda** — selalu. "A red shirt" (BUKAN "a shirt red"). "A big house" (BUKAN "a house big"). "An interesting book" (BUKAN "a book interesting"). Kalau ada beberapa kata sifat, urutannya: pendapat → ukuran → usia → warna → asal → bahan → kata benda. Contoh: "A beautiful small old red Italian leather bag."

practice.en: Flip these Indonesian phrases into English — say each one aloud: **mobil merah** → "a red car." **rumah besar** → "a big house." **film bagus** → "a good film." **orang baik** → "a kind person." **buku menarik** → "an interesting book." **kopi panas** → "hot coffee." **tas hitam** → "a black bag." Feel the adjective land BEFORE the noun.
practice.vi: Đảo các cụm tiếng Indonesia sau sang tiếng Anh — nói thành tiếng: **mobil merah** → "a red car." **rumah besar** → "a big house." **film bagus** → "a good film." **orang baik** → "a kind person." **buku menarik** → "an interesting book." **kopi panas** → "hot coffee." **tas hitam** → "a black bag." Cảm nhận tính từ nằm TRƯỚC danh từ.
practice.ja: インドネシア語のフレーズを英語にひっくり返して、声に出しましょう：**mobil merah** → 「a red car.」**rumah besar** → 「a big house.」**film bagus** → 「a good film.」**orang baik** → 「a kind person.」**buku menarik** → 「an interesting book.」**kopi panas** → 「hot coffee.」**tas hitam** → 「a black bag.」形容詞が名詞の前に来る感覚をつかみましょう。
practice.id: Balik frasa bahasa Indonesia ini ke bahasa Inggris — ucapkan setiap kali dengan keras: **mobil merah** → "a red car." **rumah besar** → "a big house." **film bagus** → "a good film." **orang baik** → "a kind person." **buku menarik** → "an interesting book." **kopi panas** → "hot coffee." **tas hitam** → "a black bag." Rasakan kata sifat mendarat SEBELUM kata benda.

takeaway.en: Adjective before noun — ALWAYS. "A red shirt" ✓, "A shirt red" ✗. This is a full reversal from Indonesian.
takeaway.vi: Tính từ trước danh từ — LUÔN LUÔN. "A red shirt" ✓, "A shirt red" ✗. Đây là sự đảo ngược hoàn toàn so với tiếng Indonesia.
takeaway.ja: 形容詞は名詞の前 — 常に。「A red shirt」✓、「A shirt red」✗。インドネシア語とは完全に逆です。
takeaway.id: Kata sifat sebelum kata benda — SELALU. "A red shirt" ✓, "A shirt red" ✗. Ini pembalikan total dari bahasa Indonesia.

hook.en: Sound familiar? "She go to school every day." Almost every Vietnamese learner says this — and the fix is one tiny letter.
hook.vi: Nghe quen không? "She go to school every day." Gần như bạn nào học tiếng Anh ban đầu cũng nói y vậy — mà cách sửa chỉ là **một chữ cái thôi**.
hook.ja: 「She go to school every day.」と言っていませんか？日本語も動詞は主語で変化しません。「彼女は行く」も「私は行く」も同じ「行く」。だから英語の **-s** は、日本語話者にとっても盲点です。
hook.id: Pernah dengar? "She go to school every day." Hampir semua pelajar Indonesia mengatakan ini — dan perbaikannya cuma satu huruf kecil.

why.en: In Vietnamese, the verb never changes. "Tôi đi", "cô ấy đi", "chúng tôi đi" — same **đi**. So your ear doesn't expect the verb to move when the subject changes.
why.vi: Tiếng Việt mình động từ không bao giờ đổi. "Tôi đi", "cô ấy đi", "chúng tôi đi" — vẫn là **đi**. Nên tai của bạn không quen với việc động từ phải đổi khi chủ ngữ đổi.
why.ja: 日本語も同じです。「私は行く」「彼女は行く」「みんな行く」— 動詞「行く」は変わりません。でも英語は、主語が **he / she / it** のとき、動詞に **-s** を付けないと不自然に聞こえます。これは日本語にないルールなので、意識しないと絶対に忘れます。
why.id: Dalam bahasa Indonesia, kata kerja tidak pernah berubah. "Saya pergi", "dia pergi", "kami pergi" — tetap **pergi**. Jadi telinga kamu tidak terbiasa dengan kata kerja yang berubah saat subjek berubah.

pattern.en: When the subject is **he**, **she**, or **it** (or anything you could replace with one of those — "my brother", "the train", "Lan"), add **-s** to the verb. "He works." "The train leaves." "Lan watches TV."
pattern.vi: Khi chủ ngữ là **he**, **she**, **it** (hoặc bất cứ từ nào có thể thay bằng một trong ba — "my brother", "the train", "Lan"), thì thêm **-s** vào động từ. "He works." "The train leaves." "Lan watches TV."
pattern.ja: 主語が **he / she / it**（またはそれで言い換えられるもの —「my brother」「the train」「Lan」など）のとき、動詞に **-s** を付けます。「He works.」「The train leaves.」「Lan watches TV.」語尾が **-ch, -sh, -s, -x, -o** の動詞は **-es** を付けます（watch → watches, go → goes）。**子音 + y** は **-ies** に変わります（study → studies）。
pattern.id: Saat subjeknya **he**, **she**, atau **it** (atau apa pun yang bisa diganti dengan salah satunya — "my brother", "the train", "Lan"), tambahkan **-s** ke kata kerja. "He works." "The train leaves." "Lan watches TV."

practice.en: Say each of these out loud before reading the answer — your mouth has to learn the **-s** sound at the end. "My father drives a taxi." "The baby cries a lot." "She doesn't like coffee." Notice negatives use **doesn't**, not **don't**.
practice.vi: Hãy nói thành tiếng từng câu sau trước khi xem đáp án — miệng phải làm quen với âm **-s** ở cuối. "My father drives a taxi." "The baby cries a lot." "She doesn't like coffee." Để ý câu phủ định dùng **doesn't**, không phải **don't**.
practice.ja: 声に出して練習しましょう。語尾の **-s** の音に口を慣らすのがポイントです。「My father drives a taxi.」「The baby cries a lot.」「She doesn't like coffee.」否定文では **don't** ではなく **doesn't** を使います。**doesn't** に **-s** が付いているので、動詞は原形のまま（doesn't like ✅、doesn't likes ❌）。
practice.id: Ucapkan setiap kalimat ini dengan keras sebelum membaca jawabannya — mulut kamu harus belajar bunyi **-s** di akhir. "My father drives a taxi." "The baby cries a lot." "She doesn't like coffee." Perhatikan kalimat negatif menggunakan **doesn't**, bukan **don't**.

takeaway.en: He / she / it → verb gets **-s**. Say it slowly until the **-s** lands naturally.
takeaway.vi: He / she / it → động từ có **-s**. Nói chậm cho đến khi âm **-s** ra tự nhiên.
takeaway.ja: He / she / it → 動詞に **-s**。ゆっくり発音して、語尾の **-s** が自然に出るまで練習しましょう。
takeaway.id: He / she / it → kata kerja dapat **-s**. Ucapkan pelan-pelan sampai bunyi **-s** keluar dengan alami.

title.en: Past tense — change the verb, not just the time
title.vi: Quá khứ — phải đổi động từ, không chỉ đổi thời gian

hook.en: "Yesterday I work late." Sounds fine in Vietnamese logic — "hôm qua" already says past, right? In English that's not enough. The verb has to move too.
hook.vi: "Yesterday I work late." Nghe theo lối tiếng Việt thì hợp lý — đã có "hôm qua" rồi mà, đúng không? Nhưng tiếng Anh chưa đủ. Động từ phải đổi luôn.
hook.ja: 「Yesterday I work late.」— 日本語でも「昨日」があれば過去だと分かりますよね。でも英語は「yesterday」だけでは不十分。動詞そのものを過去形に変えないと、ネイティブには不自然に聞こえます。日本語の「〜ました／〜た」を必ず付ける感覚に近いです。
hook.id: "Yesterday I work late." Kedengarannya masuk akal dalam logika bahasa Indonesia — "kemarin" sudah menunjukkan lampau, kan? Dalam bahasa Inggris itu tidak cukup. Kata kerjanya juga harus berubah.

why.en: Vietnamese signals time with words like **đã**, **hôm qua**, **năm ngoái** — the verb stays the same. English forces the verb itself to carry the past tense, even when a time word is already there.
why.vi: Tiếng Việt mình báo thời gian bằng từ như **đã**, **hôm qua**, **năm ngoái** — động từ vẫn giữ nguyên. Tiếng Anh thì bắt động từ phải tự mang dấu hiệu quá khứ, dù đã có từ chỉ thời gian rồi.
why.ja: 日本語には「〜ました／〜た」という過去形がありますが、英語の過去形はさらに厳格です。日本語では「昨日、遅くまで働く」のように時間詞で示せば通じることもありますが、英語では時間詞があっても動詞は必ず過去形にします。「yesterday」＋「work」の組み合わせは絶対にダメ。「yesterday」＋「worked」が正解です。
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia menandai waktu dengan kata seperti **sudah**, **kemarin**, **tahun lalu** — kata kerjanya tetap sama. Bahasa Inggris memaksa kata kerjanya sendiri yang membawa bentuk lampau, meskipun kata waktu sudah ada.

pattern.en: Regular verbs: add **-ed** (work → worked, call → called). Verbs ending in consonant + **-y**: change to **-ied** (study → studied). Irregular verbs you have to memorize: go → went, eat → ate, see → saw.
pattern.vi: Động từ thường: thêm **-ed** (work → worked, call → called). Phụ âm + **-y**: đổi thành **-ied** (study → studied). Bất quy tắc thì phải học thuộc: go → went, eat → ate, see → saw.
pattern.ja: 規則動詞は **-ed** を付けます（work → worked, call → called）。語尾が **子音 + y** のときは **-ied** に変わります（study → studied）。不規則動詞は暗記が必要です：go → went, eat → ate, see → saw。日本語にも「する→した」「来る→来た」のような不規則変化がありますよね。同じ感覚で覚えましょう。
pattern.id: Kata kerja beraturan: tambahkan **-ed** (work → worked, call → called). Kata kerja berakhiran konsonan + **-y**: ubah menjadi **-ied** (study → studied). Kata kerja tidak beraturan harus dihafal: go → went, eat → ate, see → saw.

practice.en: Try these aloud: "Yesterday I worked late." "She called me last night." "We went to Hanoi last summer." "He studied for three hours." Listen for the **-ed** sound — sometimes it's /t/ (worked), sometimes /d/ (called), sometimes /id/ (visited).
practice.vi: Nói thành tiếng: "Yesterday I worked late." "She called me last night." "We went to Hanoi last summer." "He studied for three hours." Nghe kỹ âm **-ed** — có khi là /t/ (worked), có khi là /d/ (called), có khi là /id/ (visited).
practice.ja: 声に出して練習：「Yesterday I worked late.」「She called me last night.」「We went to Hanoi last summer.」「He studied for three hours.」**-ed** の発音は3種類あります：/t/（worked）、/d/（called）、/ɪd/（visited）。日本語話者は最後の /ɪd/ を忘れがちなので注意。
practice.id: Coba ucapkan dengan keras: "Yesterday I worked late." "She called me last night." "We went to Hanoi last summer." "He studied for three hours." Dengarkan bunyi **-ed** — kadang bunyinya /t/ (worked), kadang /d/ (called), kadang /id/ (visited).

takeaway.en: A time word alone is not enough. If it happened in the past, **change the verb** — every time.
takeaway.vi: Có từ chỉ thời gian thôi chưa đủ. Nếu việc đã xảy ra trong quá khứ, **phải đổi động từ** — mỗi lần đều phải đổi.
takeaway.ja: 時間を表す言葉だけでは不十分。過去のことを言うときは、必ず動詞も過去形に。日本語の「〜ました／〜た」を付けるのと同じ習慣で。
takeaway.id: Kata waktu saja tidak cukup. Kalau kejadiannya di masa lampau, **ubah kata kerjanya** — setiap kali.

explanation.en: Past negative uses **didn't** + bare verb: **didn't come**, not **didn't came**.
explanation.vi: Phủ định quá khứ dùng **didn't** + động từ nguyên mẫu: **didn't come**, không phải **didn't came**.
explanation.ja: 過去の否定は **didn't** + 動詞の原形：**didn't come**（**didn't came** ではない）。**didn't** が過去を表すので、動詞は原形のまま。これは日本語話者がよく間違えるポイントです。
explanation.id: Negatif lampau menggunakan **didn't** + kata kerja dasar: **didn't come**, bukan **didn't came**.

hook.en: "She a teacher." "I tired." "They at home." Every Vietnamese learner says these in their first English month. The missing word is tiny — **be** — but English insists on it.
hook.vi: "She a teacher." "I tired." "They at home." Bạn nào học tiếng Anh tháng đầu cũng nói vậy. Từ thiếu rất nhỏ — **be** — mà tiếng Anh thì bắt buộc phải có.
hook.ja: 「She a teacher.」「I tired.」「They at home.」— 日本語話者も初級でよくやってしまうミスです。日本語では「彼女は先生」で文が成立しますが、英語は **be動詞** がないと文として成り立ちません。**am / is / are** は絶対に必要です。
hook.id: "She a teacher." "I tired." "They at home." Setiap pelajar Indonesia mengatakan ini di bulan pertama belajar bahasa Inggris. Kata yang hilang sangat kecil — **be** — tapi bahasa Inggris mewajibkannya.

why.en: Vietnamese says "Cô ấy giáo viên" — no verb in the middle. English doesn't allow that. Between a subject and a description (adjective, noun, place), you need **am**, **is**, or **are**.
why.vi: Tiếng Việt mình nói "Cô ấy giáo viên" — không có động từ ở giữa. Tiếng Anh không cho phép. Giữa chủ ngữ và phần mô tả (tính từ, danh từ, nơi chốn), phải có **am**, **is**, hoặc **are**.
why.ja: 日本語も「彼女は先生」で通じます。しかし英語では、主語と説明（形容詞・名詞・場所）の間に必ず **be動詞** が必要です。日本語の「〜です・〜だ」に近い役割ですが、英語の be動詞はもっと厳格で、省略できません。特に形容詞の前（「I am tired」—「疲れた」は日本語では動詞扱い）は忘れやすいので注意。
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia mengatakan "Dia guru" — tidak ada kata kerja di tengahnya. Bahasa Inggris tidak mengizinkan itu. Di antara subjek dan deskripsi (kata sifat, kata benda, tempat), kamu perlu **am**, **is**, atau **are**.

pattern.en: **I → am**, **you / we / they → are**, **he / she / it → is**. Past forms: **I / he / she / it → was**, **you / we / they → were**. Use them whenever there's no other action verb in the sentence.
pattern.vi: **I → am**, **you / we / they → are**, **he / she / it → is**. Quá khứ: **I / he / she / it → was**, **you / we / they → were**. Dùng khi câu không có động từ chỉ hành động nào khác.
pattern.ja: **I → am**、**you / we / they → are**、**he / she / it → is**。過去形：**I / he / she / it → was**、**you / we / they → were**。文に他の動作動詞がないときは、必ず be動詞を入れます。「She tired.」ではなく「She **is** tired.」です。
pattern.id: **I → am**, **you / we / they → are**, **he / she / it → is**. Bentuk lampau: **I / he / she / it → was**, **you / we / they → were**. Gunakan saat tidak ada kata kerja aksi lain di kalimat.

practice.en: Say each one out loud and feel the **be** sit in the middle of the sentence: "She is a teacher." "I am tired." "They are at home." "He was kind yesterday." "My parents are at work."
practice.vi: Nói thành tiếng và cảm nhận **be** nằm giữa câu: "She is a teacher." "I am tired." "They are at home." "He was kind yesterday." "My parents are at work."
practice.ja: 声に出して、be動詞が文の中心にある感覚をつかみましょう：「She is a teacher.」「I am tired.」「They are at home.」「He was kind yesterday.」「My parents are at work.」日本語の「〜です」よりも be動詞の方が文の中で重みがあります。
practice.id: Ucapkan setiap kalimat dengan keras dan rasakan **be** duduk di tengah kalimat: "She is a teacher." "I am tired." "They are at home." "He was kind yesterday." "My parents are at work."

takeaway.en: If your sentence has no action verb, **be** is the verb. Add it every time.
takeaway.vi: Nếu câu không có động từ chỉ hành động, **be** chính là động từ. Lần nào cũng phải thêm vào.
takeaway.ja: 文に動作動詞がないときは、**be動詞** が主役の動詞です。毎回必ず入れましょう。「彼女は先生」→「She **is** a teacher.」
takeaway.id: Kalau kalimatmu tidak punya kata kerja aksi, **be** adalah kata kerjanya. Tambahkan setiap kali.

title.vi: If + quá khứ → **would**, không bao giờ **will**

hook.en: "If I had money, I will buy a car." Every Indonesian learner writes this. In Indonesian, **kalau** doesn't change the verb — but English has a strict tense pattern for unreal situations.
hook.vi: "If I had money, I will buy a car." Bạn học người Việt nào cũng từng viết câu này. Tiếng Việt mình **nếu...thì...** không đổi động từ — nhưng tiếng Anh có quy tắc thì nghiêm ngặt cho tình huống không có thật.
hook.ja: 「If I had money, I will buy a car.」— 日本語の「〜たら」「〜ば」は現実でも非現実でも動詞が変わりません。でも英語では非現実の条件には決まった時制の組み合わせがあります。
hook.id: "If I had money, I will buy a car." Setiap pelajar Indonesia pernah menulis ini. Dalam bahasa Indonesia, **kalau** tidak mengubah kata kerja — tapi bahasa Inggris punya pola tenses yang ketat untuk situasi yang tidak nyata.

why.en: Indonesian uses **kalau...maka...** and the verb stays the same whether the condition is real or imagined. English marks the difference: real condition → **If + present, will + V**; unreal condition → **If + past, would + V**. Never mix **past** with **will**.
why.vi: Tiếng Việt dùng **nếu...thì...** và động từ không đổi dù điều kiện có thật hay không. Tiếng Anh phân biệt: điều kiện có thật → **If + hiện tại, will + V**; điều kiện không có thật → **If + quá khứ, would + V**. Đừng bao giờ trộn **quá khứ** với **will**.
why.ja: 日本語の「もし〜たら」は条件が現実的でも非現実的でも動詞の形が同じです。英語は区別します：現実的条件 → **If + 現在形, will + V**；非現実的条件 → **If + 過去形, would + V**。過去形と **will** を混ぜてはいけません。
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia menggunakan **kalau...maka...** dan kata kerjanya tetap sama baik kondisi itu nyata maupun tidak. Bahasa Inggris menandai perbedaannya: kondisi nyata → **If + present, will + V**; kondisi tidak nyata → **If + past, would + V**. Jangan pernah mencampur **past** dengan **will**.

pattern.en: Type 1 (real/possible): **If I have money, I will buy a car.** Type 2 (unreal/imagined): **If I had money, I would buy a car.** The **past tense** in the if-clause signals the situation is imagined, not past time.
pattern.vi: Loại 1 (có thật/có thể): **If I have money, I will buy a car.** Loại 2 (không thật/tưởng tượng): **If I had money, I would buy a car.** Thì **quá khứ** trong mệnh đề if báo hiệu tình huống là tưởng tượng, không phải thời gian quá khứ.
pattern.ja: タイプ1（現実的）：**If I have money, I will buy a car.** タイプ2（非現実的）：**If I had money, I would buy a car.** if節の**過去形**は「過去の時間」ではなく「現実でない仮定」を表します。
pattern.id: Tipe 1 (nyata/mungkin): **If I have money, I will buy a car.** Tipe 2 (tidak nyata/khayalan): **If I had money, I would buy a car.** **Past tense** di klausa if menandakan situasinya hanya khayalan, bukan waktu lampau.

practice.en: Say each aloud: "If I study, I will pass." (real plan) vs "If I studied, I would pass." (I'm not studying now). "If she comes, we will start." (real) vs "If she came, we would start." (she probably won't come). Feel the shift from **will** to **would**.
practice.vi: Nói thành tiếng: "If I study, I will pass." (kế hoạch thật) vs "If I studied, I would pass." (tôi đang không học). "If she comes, we will start." (thật) vs "If she came, we would start." (cô ấy chắc không đến). Cảm nhận sự chuyển từ **will** sang **would**.
practice.ja: 声に出して：「If I study, I will pass.」（現実的）vs「If I studied, I would pass.」（今勉強していない仮定）。「If she comes, we will start.」（現実的）vs「If she came, we would start.」（彼女は多分来ない）。**will** から **would** への切り替えを意識して。
practice.id: Ucapkan dengan keras: "If I study, I will pass." (rencana nyata) vs "If I studied, I would pass." (saya tidak sedang belajar sekarang). "If she comes, we will start." (nyata) vs "If she came, we would start." (dia mungkin tidak akan datang). Rasakan peralihan dari **will** ke **would**.

takeaway.en: Imagined situation → If + **past**, **would** + V. Never **will** after a past if-clause.
takeaway.vi: Tình huống tưởng tượng → If + **quá khứ**, **would** + V. Không bao giờ **will** sau mệnh đề if quá khứ.
takeaway.ja: 非現実の仮定 → If + **過去形**, **would** + V。過去のif節の後ろに **will** は絶対に置かない。
takeaway.id: Situasi khayalan → If + **past**, **would** + V. Jangan pernah pakai **will** setelah klausa if bentuk lampau.

question.en: Choose the correct unreal conditional:
question.vi: Chọn câu điều kiện không thật đúng:

options: If I have money, I will buy a car.
If I had money, I will buy a car.
If I had money, I would buy a car.
If I have money, I would buy a car.
quiz.correctAnswer: If I had money, I would buy a car.

explanation.en: Unreal (I don't have money now) → If + **past** + **would**.
explanation.vi: Không thật (tôi không có tiền bây giờ) → If + **quá khứ** + **would**.
explanation.ja: 非現実（今お金がない）→ If + **過去形** + **would**。
explanation.id: Tidak nyata (saya tidak punya uang sekarang) → If + **past** + **would**.

question.en: Fill in: If she ___ here, she would help us.

explanation.en: Unreal condition → if-clause uses **past** tense: **was** (or **were**).
explanation.vi: Điều kiện không thật → mệnh đề if dùng thì **quá khứ**: **was** (hoặc **were**).
explanation.ja: 非現実の条件 → if節は**過去形**：**was**（または **were**）。
explanation.id: Kondisi tidak nyata → klausa if pakai **past** tense: **was** (atau **were**).

If I know the answer, I will tell you.

If I known the answer, I will tell you.

explanation.en: Real/possible → **If + present, will + V**.
explanation.vi: Có thật/khả thi → **If + hiện tại, will + V**.
explanation.ja: 現実的/可能 → **If + 現在形, will + V**。

question.en: What is wrong? If I would be you, I would take the job.

explanation.en: The if-clause never uses **would**. Use past: **If I were you, I would take the job.**
explanation.vi: Mệnh đề if không bao giờ dùng **would**. Dùng quá khứ: **If I were you, I would take the job.**
explanation.ja: if節に **would** は使えません。過去形で：**If I were you, I would take the job.**
explanation.id: Klausa if tidak pernah pakai **would**. Pakai past: **If I were you, I would take the job.**

question.en: Fill in: If I ___ taller, I would play basketball.

explanation.en: Imagined situation (I'm not tall now) → **If + past, would + V**.
explanation.vi: Tình huống tưởng tượng (tôi không cao bây giờ) → **If + quá khứ, would + V**.

title.en: Reported speech — shift the tense back
title.vi: Câu tường thuật — lùi thì một bậc

hook.en: "She said she is tired." Natural in Indonesian — you just quote what the person said. But English demands a tense shift. What she said happened in the past, so the verb moves back one step.
hook.vi: "She said she is tired." Tự nhiên trong tiếng Việt — bạn chỉ cần thuật lại lời người ta nói. Nhưng tiếng Anh đòi hỏi lùi thì. Những gì cô ấy nói đã ở quá khứ, nên động từ phải lùi về một bậc.
hook.ja: 「She said she is tired.」— 日本語の「〜と言った」では、言った内容の時制は変わりません。でも英語では、伝える内容の時制を一つ過去にずらします。
hook.id: "She said she is tired." Wajar dalam bahasa Indonesia — kamu tinggal mengutip apa yang orang katakan. Tapi bahasa Inggris menuntut pergeseran tenses. Apa yang dia katakan sudah terjadi di masa lalu, jadi kata kerjanya mundur satu langkah.

why.en: Indonesian reports speech directly or with **katanya** / **dia bilang** — the verb tense stays exactly as it was spoken. English shifts the tense back: present → past, past → past perfect, will → would. This is called **backshifting**.
why.vi: Tiếng Việt thuật lại lời nói trực tiếp hoặc dùng **nói rằng** / **bảo là** — thì của động từ giữ nguyên. Tiếng Anh lùi thì một bậc: hiện tại → quá khứ, quá khứ → quá khứ hoàn thành, will → would. Đây gọi là **backshifting**.
why.ja: 日本語は「〜と言った」で直接引用しても間接引用しても動詞の形が変わりません。英語では**時制の一致**が起こり、伝える内容の動詞を一つ過去にずらします：現在→過去、過去→過去完了、will→would。
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia melaporkan ucapan secara langsung atau dengan **katanya** / **dia bilang** — tenses kata kerjanya tetap sama seperti saat diucapkan. Bahasa Inggris menggeser tenses mundur: present → past, past → past perfect, will → would. Ini disebut **backshifting**.

pattern.en: Direct: She said, "I **am** tired." → Reported: She said she **was** tired. Direct: He said, "I **will** call you." → Reported: He said he **would** call me. Direct: They said, "We **went** to the market." → Reported: They said they **had gone** to the market.
pattern.vi: Trực tiếp: She said, "I **am** tired." → Thuật lại: She said she **was** tired. Trực tiếp: He said, "I **will** call you." → Thuật lại: He said he **would** call me. Trực tiếp: They said, "We **went** to the market." → Thuật lại: They said they **had gone** to the market.
pattern.ja: 直接話法：She said, "I **am** tired." → 間接話法：She said she **was** tired。直接：He said, "I **will** call you." → 間接：He said he **would** call me。直接：They said, "We **went** to the market." → 間接：They said they **had gone** to the market。
pattern.id: Langsung: She said, "I **am** tired." → Tidak langsung: She said she **was** tired. Langsung: He said, "I **will** call you." → Tidak langsung: He said he **would** call me. Langsung: They said, "We **went** to the market." → Tidak langsung: They said they **had gone** to the market.

practice.en: Convert these aloud: "I like coffee" → He said he **liked** coffee. "I am working" → She said she **was working**. "I will come" → He said he **would come**. "I have finished" → She said she **had finished**. Feel the one-step-back shift.
practice.vi: Chuyển đổi thành tiếng: "I like coffee" → He said he **liked** coffee. "I am working" → She said she **was working**. "I will come" → He said he **would come**. "I have finished" → She said she **had finished**. Cảm nhận bước lùi một thì.
practice.ja: 声に出して変換：「I like coffee」→ He said he **liked** coffee。「I am working」→ She said she **was working**。「I will come」→ He said he **would come**。「I have finished」→ She said she **had finished**。一段階ずつ時制が下がる感覚をつかみましょう。
practice.id: Ubah dengan keras: "I like coffee" → He said he **liked** coffee. "I am working" → She said she **was working**. "I will come" → He said he **would come**. "I have finished" → She said she **had finished**. Rasakan pergeseran mundur satu langkah.

takeaway.en: Reported speech = take the original verb and move it back one tense step. Every time.
takeaway.vi: Câu tường thuật = lấy động từ gốc và lùi về một bậc thì. Lần nào cũng vậy.
takeaway.ja: 間接話法 = 元の動詞を時制で一段階戻す。毎回必ず。
takeaway.id: Kalimat tidak langsung = ambil kata kerja aslinya dan mundurkan satu langkah tenses. Setiap kali.

title.en: **I have done** vs **I did** — picking the right past
title.vi: **I have done** vs **I did** — chọn đúng thì quá khứ
title.id: **I have done** vs **I did** — memilih bentuk lampau yang tepat

hook.en: Sound familiar? "I have eaten breakfast this morning." In Indonesian logic this makes perfect sense — you use **sudah** for anything that's done. But in English, the moment you name a specific past time like "this morning," you need simple past — not present perfect.
hook.vi: Nghe quen không? "I have eaten breakfast this morning." Trong logic tiếng Indonesia điều này hoàn toàn hợp lý — bạn dùng **sudah** cho mọi thứ đã xong. Nhưng trong tiếng Anh, ngay khi bạn nêu thời gian cụ thể như "this morning," bạn phải dùng simple past — không phải present perfect.
hook.id: Pernah dengar? "I have eaten breakfast this morning." Dalam logika bahasa Indonesia ini masuk akal — kamu pakai **sudah** untuk semua yang sudah selesai. Tapi dalam bahasa Inggris, begitu kamu menyebut waktu lampau spesifik seperti "this morning," kamu harus pakai simple past — bukan present perfect.

why.en: Indonesian uses **sudah** for all completed actions — **Saya sudah makan** can mean "I ate" or "I have eaten." English splits them: when you name a specific past time (**yesterday**, **last week**, **this morning**, **in 2020**), use simple past. When the past action still matters now and no specific time is named, use present perfect.
why.vi: Tiếng Indonesia dùng **sudah** cho mọi hành động đã hoàn thành — **Saya sudah makan** có thể là "I ate" hoặc "I have eaten." Tiếng Anh phân biệt: khi bạn nêu thời gian cụ thể trong quá khứ, dùng simple past. Khi hành động quá khứ vẫn còn liên quan đến hiện tại và không có thời gian cụ thể, dùng present perfect.
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia menggunakan **sudah** untuk semua tindakan selesai — **Saya sudah makan** bisa berarti "I ate" atau "I have eaten." Bahasa Inggris membedakannya: saat kamu menyebut waktu lampau spesifik (**yesterday**, **last week**, **this morning**, **in 2020**), gunakan simple past. Saat tindakan lampau masih relevan sekarang dan tidak ada waktu spesifik, gunakan present perfect.

pattern.en: **Simple past** = specific past time named → verb in past form. "I ate breakfast this morning." "She called yesterday." **Present perfect** = result still relevant, no specific time → **have/has + V3**. "I have eaten (so I'm not hungry now)." "She has lost her keys (still can't find them)." **Key test:** can you add **yesterday / last / ago / in [year]** to the sentence? If yes → simple past, not present perfect.
pattern.vi: **Simple past** = thời gian quá khứ cụ thể → động từ dạng quá khứ. "I ate breakfast this morning." "She called yesterday." **Present perfect** = kết quả vẫn còn liên quan, không có thời gian cụ thể → **have/has + V3**. "I have eaten (nên giờ không đói)." "She has lost her keys (vẫn chưa tìm thấy)." **Cách kiểm tra:** bạn có thêm được **yesterday / last / ago / in [năm]** vào câu không? Nếu có → simple past, không phải present perfect.
pattern.id: **Simple past** = waktu lampau spesifik disebut → kata kerja bentuk lampau. "I ate breakfast this morning." "She called yesterday." **Present perfect** = hasil masih relevan, tidak ada waktu spesifik → **have/has + V3**. "I have eaten (jadi sekarang tidak lapar)." "She has lost her keys (masih belum ketemu)." **Tes kunci:** bisakah kamu menambahkan **yesterday / last / ago / in [tahun]** ke kalimat? Kalau bisa → simple past, bukan present perfect.

practice.en: Say each of these out loud and feel the difference: "I have visited Jakarta." (life experience, no specific time) vs "I visited Jakarta last year." (specific time). "She has finished her homework." (just finished, still relevant) vs "She finished her homework an hour ago." (specific time). "They have bought a new car." (recent, result matters) vs "They bought a new car last month." (when is stated).
practice.vi: Nói thành tiếng và cảm nhận sự khác biệt: "I have visited Jakarta." (trải nghiệm, không thời gian cụ thể) vs "I visited Jakarta last year." (thời gian cụ thể). "She has finished her homework." (vừa xong, vẫn liên quan) vs "She finished her homework an hour ago." (thời gian cụ thể). "They have bought a new car." (gần đây, kết quả quan trọng) vs "They bought a new car last month." (có thời gian).
practice.id: Ucapkan setiap kalimat dengan keras dan rasakan bedanya: "I have visited Jakarta." (pengalaman hidup, tidak ada waktu spesifik) vs "I visited Jakarta last year." (waktu spesifik). "She has finished her homework." (baru selesai, masih relevan) vs "She finished her homework an hour ago." (waktu spesifik). "They have bought a new car." (baru terjadi, hasil penting) vs "They bought a new car last month." (waktu disebutkan).

takeaway.en: Specific past time word (yesterday, last, ago) = simple past. No time word + result still matters = present perfect.
takeaway.vi: Có từ thời gian quá khứ cụ thể = simple past. Không có từ thời gian + kết quả vẫn quan trọng = present perfect.
takeaway.id: Ada kata waktu lampau spesifik (yesterday, last, ago) = simple past. Tidak ada kata waktu + hasil masih relevan = present perfect.

title.en: **If I were** — unreal conditions in English
title.vi: **If I were** — câu điều kiện không có thật
title.id: **If I were** — pengandaian tidak nyata dalam bahasa Inggris

hook.en: Sound familiar? "If I have money, I would travel the world." In Indonesian, **kalau** works the same way whether the situation is real or imaginary — **Kalau saya punya uang, saya akan keliling dunia.** But English draws a hard line between real and unreal conditions, and mixing them sounds broken.
hook.vi: Nghe quen không? "If I have money, I would travel the world." Trong tiếng Indonesia, **kalau** hoạt động giống nhau dù tình huống có thật hay tưởng tượng. Nhưng tiếng Anh phân biệt rạch ròi giữa điều kiện thật và không thật, trộn lẫn nghe rất sai.
hook.id: Pernah dengar? "If I have money, I would travel the world." Dalam bahasa Indonesia, **kalau** bekerja sama baik untuk situasi nyata maupun khayalan — **Kalau saya punya uang, saya akan keliling dunia.** Tapi bahasa Inggris menarik garis tegas antara kondisi nyata dan tidak nyata, dan mencampurkannya terdengar rusak.

why.en: Indonesian **kalau… maka…** doesn't change the verb form for unreal situations — the same structure covers both "If it rains, I will stay home" (real) and "If I were rich, I would travel" (unreal). English marks the difference: unreal / hypothetical conditions use **If + past tense, would + base verb**. Never mix past tense in the **if**-clause with **will** in the result.
why.vi: Tiếng Indonesia **kalau… maka…** không đổi dạng động từ cho tình huống không thật — cùng một cấu trúc cho cả "Nếu trời mưa, tôi sẽ ở nhà" (thật) và "Nếu tôi giàu, tôi sẽ đi du lịch" (không thật). Tiếng Anh đánh dấu sự khác biệt: điều kiện không thật dùng **If + quá khứ, would + động từ gốc**. Không bao giờ trộn quá khứ trong mệnh đề **if** với **will** ở mệnh đề kết quả.
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia **kalau… maka…** tidak mengubah bentuk kata kerja untuk situasi tidak nyata — struktur yang sama mencakup "Kalau hujan, saya akan di rumah" (nyata) dan "Kalau saya kaya, saya akan keliling dunia" (tidak nyata). Bahasa Inggris menandai perbedaannya: kondisi tidak nyata/hipotetis menggunakan **If + past tense, would + kata kerja dasar**. Jangan pernah mencampur past tense di klausa **if** dengan **will** di hasil.

pattern.en: **Real condition (Type 1):** If + present simple, will + base verb. "If it rains, I will stay home." **Unreal condition (Type 2):** If + simple past, would + base verb. "If I **were** rich, I **would travel** the world." Note: **were** is used for ALL subjects in Type 2 (formal) — "If I **were** you," not "If I **was** you." The past form doesn't mean past time — it signals "this is imaginary."
pattern.vi: **Điều kiện thật (Type 1):** If + hiện tại, will + động từ gốc. "If it rains, I will stay home." **Điều kiện không thật (Type 2):** If + quá khứ, would + động từ gốc. "If I **were** rich, I **would travel** the world." Lưu ý: **were** dùng cho TẤT CẢ các chủ ngữ trong Type 2 (trang trọng) — "If I **were** you," không phải "If I **was** you." Dạng quá khứ không có nghĩa thời gian quá khứ — nó báo hiệu "đây là tưởng tượng."
pattern.id: **Kondisi nyata (Type 1):** If + present simple, will + kata kerja dasar. "If it rains, I will stay home." **Kondisi tidak nyata (Type 2):** If + simple past, would + kata kerja dasar. "If I **were** rich, I **would travel** the world." Catatan: **were** digunakan untuk SEMUA subjek di Type 2 (formal) — "If I **were** you," bukan "If I **was** you." Bentuk past tidak berarti waktu lampau — ini menandakan "ini khayalan."

practice.en: Say each pair out loud and feel the contrast: "If I have time tomorrow, I will call you." (real — tomorrow is possible) vs "If I had time, I would call you." (unreal — I don't have time now). "If she studies, she will pass." (real — she might study) vs "If she studied, she would pass." (unreal — she doesn't study). The past tense in the **if**-clause doesn't mean past — it means pretend.
practice.vi: Nói thành tiếng từng cặp và cảm nhận sự tương phản: "If I have time tomorrow, I will call you." (thật — ngày mai có thể) vs "If I had time, I would call you." (không thật — giờ không có thời gian). "If she studies, she will pass." (thật — có thể học) vs "If she studied, she would pass." (không thật — cô ấy không học). Thì quá khứ trong mệnh đề **if** không có nghĩa quá khứ — nó có nghĩa là giả vờ.
practice.id: Ucapkan setiap pasangan dengan keras dan rasakan kontrasnya: "If I have time tomorrow, I will call you." (nyata — besok mungkin) vs "If I had time, I would call you." (tidak nyata — sekarang tidak punya waktu). "If she studies, she will pass." (nyata — dia mungkin belajar) vs "If she studied, she would pass." (tidak nyata — dia tidak belajar). Past tense di klausa **if** bukan berarti waktu lampau — artinya pura-pura.

takeaway.en: Real = present + will. Unreal / pretend = past + would. If you hear yourself say **will** after a past-tense **if**, stop and switch to **would**.
takeaway.vi: Thật = hiện tại + will. Không thật / giả vờ = quá khứ + would. Nếu bạn nghe mình nói **will** sau mệnh đề **if** ở quá khứ, dừng lại và đổi sang **would**.
takeaway.id: Nyata = present + will. Tidak nyata / pura-pura = past + would. Kalau kamu dengar diri sendiri bilang **will** setelah klausa **if** past tense, berhenti dan ganti ke **would**.

title.en: **She said she was** — reporting speech in English
title.vi: **She said she was** — tường thuật lời nói trong tiếng Anh
title.id: **She said she was** — melaporkan ucapan dalam bahasa Inggris

hook.en: Sound familiar? "She said she is tired." In Indonesian, this is exactly right — **Dia bilang dia capek.** You just wrap the original words in **bilang** and the verb stays the same. English doesn't work that way — when you report speech, the tense takes one step back.
hook.vi: Nghe quen không? "She said she is tired." Trong tiếng Indonesia, câu này hoàn toàn đúng — **Dia bilang dia capek.** Bạn chỉ cần bọc lời gốc trong **bilang** và động từ giữ nguyên. Tiếng Anh không hoạt động như vậy — khi bạn tường thuật, thì của động từ lùi một bước.
hook.id: Pernah dengar? "She said she is tired." Dalam bahasa Indonesia, ini benar — **Dia bilang dia capek.** Kamu tinggal membungkus kata-kata asli dengan **bilang** dan kata kerjanya tetap sama. Bahasa Inggris tidak bekerja seperti itu — saat kamu melaporkan ucapan, tense mundur satu langkah.

why.en: Indonesian reports speech without changing the verb tense. **Dia bilang dia lapar** keeps present tense; **Dia bilang dia sudah makan** keeps the original form. English backshifts: if the original was present → reported becomes past; original past → reported becomes past perfect. The reporting verb **said** sets the whole sentence in the past, and the grammar follows.
why.vi: Tiếng Indonesia tường thuật không đổi thì động từ. **Dia bilang dia lapar** giữ thì hiện tại; **Dia bilang dia sudah makan** giữ dạng gốc. Tiếng Anh lùi thì: gốc là hiện tại → tường thuật thành quá khứ; gốc là quá khứ → tường thuật thành quá khứ hoàn thành. Động từ tường thuật **said** đặt cả câu vào quá khứ, và ngữ pháp đi theo.
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia melaporkan ucapan tanpa mengubah tense kata kerja. **Dia bilang dia lapar** tetap present tense; **Dia bilang dia sudah makan** tetap bentuk asli. Bahasa Inggris menggeser tense ke belakang: kalau aslinya present → reported jadi past; aslinya past → reported jadi past perfect. Kata kerja pelapor **said** menempatkan seluruh kalimat di masa lalu, dan tata bahasanya mengikuti.

pattern.en: **Backshift rule:** present → past, past → past perfect, **will** → **would**, **can** → **could**. "I am tired" → She said she **was** tired. "I went there" → She said she **had gone** there. "I will call" → She said she **would** call. **No backshift** when: the reported fact is still true now, or the reporting verb is present tense (**she says...**).
pattern.vi: **Quy tắc lùi thì:** hiện tại → quá khứ, quá khứ → quá khứ hoàn thành, **will** → **would**, **can** → **could**. "I am tired" → She said she **was** tired. "I went there" → She said she **had gone** there. "I will call" → She said she **would** call. **Không lùi thì** khi: sự thật được tường thuật vẫn đúng ở hiện tại, hoặc động từ tường thuật ở thì hiện tại (**she says...**).
pattern.id: **Aturan pergeseran tense:** present → past, past → past perfect, **will** → **would**, **can** → **could**. "I am tired" → She said she **was** tired. "I went there" → She said she **had gone** there. "I will call" → She said she **would** call. **Tidak ada pergeseran** saat: fakta yang dilaporkan masih benar sekarang, atau kata kerja pelapor dalam present tense (**she says...**).

practice.en: Practice the backshift out loud: Original: "I like coffee" → Reported: "She said she **liked** coffee." Original: "I am working" → Reported: "He said he **was** working." Original: "We saw the movie" → Reported: "They said they **had seen** the movie." Original: "I will help you" → Reported: "She said she **would** help me." The shift happens automatically once your ear expects it.
practice.vi: Luyện lùi thì thành tiếng: Gốc: "I like coffee" → Tường thuật: "She said she **liked** coffee." Gốc: "I am working" → Tường thuật: "He said he **was** working." Gốc: "We saw the movie" → Tường thuật: "They said they **had seen** the movie." Gốc: "I will help you" → Tường thuật: "She said she **would** help me." Việc lùi thì diễn ra tự động khi tai bạn đã quen.
practice.id: Latih pergeseran tense dengan keras: Asli: "I like coffee" → Dilaporkan: "She said she **liked** coffee." Asli: "I am working" → Dilaporkan: "He said he **was** working." Asli: "We saw the movie" → Dilaporkan: "They said they **had seen** the movie." Asli: "I will help you" → Dilaporkan: "She said she **would** help me." Pergeseran terjadi otomatis begitu telingamu terbiasa.

takeaway.en: Reporting verb in past tense (**said**, **told**) → shift everything one step back. Present becomes past. Past becomes past perfect. **Will** becomes **would**.
takeaway.vi: Động từ tường thuật ở quá khứ (**said**, **told**) → lùi mọi thứ một bước. Hiện tại thành quá khứ. Quá khứ thành quá khứ hoàn thành. **Will** thành **would**.
takeaway.id: Kata kerja pelapor dalam past tense (**said**, **told**) → geser semuanya satu langkah ke belakang. Present jadi past. Past jadi past perfect. **Will** jadi **would**.

hook.en: "The letter written yesterday." Almost every Indonesian learner writes this — because "surat itu ditulis kemarin" is already a complete sentence in Indonesian. But English needs one more word.
hook.vi: "The letter written yesterday." Hầu như bạn học Indonesia nào cũng viết vậy — vì "surat itu ditulis kemarin" đã là câu hoàn chỉnh trong tiếng Indonesia. Nhưng tiếng Anh cần thêm một từ nữa.
hook.ja: 「The letter written yesterday.」— 日本語の「手紙は昨日書かれた」の感覚で書いてしまいがちです。しかし英語の受動態には、必ず **be動詞** が必要です。
hook.id: "The letter written yesterday." Hampir semua pelajar Indonesia menulis seperti ini — karena "surat itu ditulis kemarin" sudah kalimat lengkap dalam bahasa Indonesia. Tapi bahasa Inggris butuh satu kata lagi.

why.en: Indonesian forms the passive with the **di-** prefix (ditulis, dimakan, dibangun). One word is enough. English needs two pieces: a form of **be** + the past participle (V3). Without **be**, the sentence sounds broken to a native ear.
why.vi: Tiếng Indonesia tạo bị động bằng tiền tố **di-** (ditulis, dimakan, dibangun). Một từ là đủ. Tiếng Anh cần hai phần: dạng **be** + quá khứ phân từ (V3). Thiếu **be**, câu nghe như gãy với tai người bản xứ.
why.ja: 日本語の受身（「〜れる」「〜られる」）は動詞の語尾変化で表します。英語の受動態は **be動詞 + 過去分詞** の2語で作り、**be動詞** を省略することは絶対にできません。
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia membentuk pasif dengan awalan **di-** (ditulis, dimakan, dibangun). Satu kata sudah cukup. Bahasa Inggris perlu dua bagian: bentuk **be** + past participle (V3). Tanpa **be**, kalimatnya terdengar patah bagi penutur asli.

pattern.en: English passive = **be + past participle (V3)**. Present: **is/are + written**. Past: **was/were + written**. Present perfect: **has/have been + written**. Future: **will be + written**. **The letter was written yesterday.** **The food is cooked every morning.** **The bridge will be built next year.**
pattern.vi: Bị động tiếng Anh = **be + quá khứ phân từ (V3)**. Hiện tại: **is/are + written**. Quá khứ: **was/were + written**. Hiện tại hoàn thành: **has/have been + written**. Tương lai: **will be + written**. **The letter was written yesterday.** **The food is cooked every morning.** **The bridge will be built next year.**
pattern.ja: 英語の受動態 = **be + 過去分詞（V3）**。現在：**is/are + written**。過去：**was/were + written**。現在完了：**has/have been + written**。未来：**will be + written**。**The letter was written yesterday.**（手紙は昨日書かれた）**The food is cooked every morning.**（料理は毎朝作られる）**The bridge will be built next year.**（橋は来年建設される）
pattern.id: Pasif bahasa Inggris = **be + past participle (V3)**. Present: **is/are + written**. Past: **was/were + written**. Present perfect: **has/have been + written**. Future: **will be + written**. **The letter was written yesterday.** **The food is cooked every morning.** **The bridge will be built next year.**

practice.en: Say each aloud and feel the **be** sitting in the middle: "The letter was written yesterday." (NOT "The letter written yesterday.") "The food is prepared fresh daily." "English is spoken here." "The work was finished on time." "A new mall will be built here."
practice.vi: Nói thành tiếng và cảm nhận **be** nằm giữa câu: "The letter was written yesterday." (KHÔNG phải "The letter written yesterday.") "The food is prepared fresh daily." "English is spoken here." "The work was finished on time." "A new mall will be built here."
practice.ja: 声に出して、**be動詞** が文の中心にある感覚をつかみましょう：「The letter was written yesterday.」（「The letter written yesterday.」ではない）「The food is prepared fresh daily.」「English is spoken here.」「The work was finished on time.」「A new mall will be built here.」
practice.id: Ucapkan setiap kalimat dengan keras dan rasakan **be** duduk di tengahnya: "The letter was written yesterday." (BUKAN "The letter written yesterday.") "The food is prepared fresh daily." "English is spoken here." "The work was finished on time." "A new mall will be built here."

takeaway.en: Passive = **be + V3**. Always. The **be** is never optional.
takeaway.vi: Bị động = **be + V3**. Luôn luôn. Không bao giờ được bỏ **be**.
takeaway.ja: 受動態 = **be + 過去分詞**。常に。**be動詞** は絶対に省略不可。
takeaway.id: Pasif = **be + V3**. Selalu. **be** tidak pernah opsional.
